about: In the priest-alone form of Mass, this prayer is said quietly before the first Gospel. It connects the request for a purified heart and lips with the cleansing of Isaiah’s lips.

seg.tr: Cleanse my heart and my lips, almighty God, who cleansed the lips of the prophet Isaiah with a glowing stone. In the same way, be pleased to cleanse me through Your gracious mercy, so that I can proclaim Your holy Gospel worthily.

a.g: cleansed the lips of Isaiah the prophet with a glowing stone
be pleased to cleanse me through Your gracious mercy
I can proclaim Your holy Gospel worthily

ex.w013: The Latin text of Isaiah 6:6–7 describes a seraph taking a stone from the altar with tongs and touching the prophet’s lips. The prayer recalls that cleansing as the model for the minister’s petition.
ex.w019: Grata describes the mercy being sought as welcome and favorable, not as grateful. It does not portray God as thanking the person who prays.
ex.w021: The petition appeals to God’s willingness to cleanse. It does not claim that the speaker has earned cleansing.

nt.w015: Igníto can be read either as a participle of ígnio, “to make red-hot,” or as the adjective ignítus, “glowing.” The stone’s heated state is clear in either reading. The phrase does not narrate a separate act of heating or identify its agent.
